newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST - U.S. Q4 sales began at moderate pace.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - U.S. Q4 sales began at moderate pace.

text.p: Sales at U.S. department stores, auto dealers, restaurants, gas stations and other retail outlets occurred at a very moderate pace in October, economists forecast.
Economists polled by Reuters offered an average estimate of a 0.3 percent retail sales gain in October after a 0.7 percent overall September increase.
The expected small increase left wide open the question of whether consumers would pick up their spending pace enough in November and December to give the fourth quarter economy a significant boost.
Retail sales have been sluggish for months, a fact some economists try to explain by pointing to consumers' high credit card balances.

But many economists expect that inhibition to weaken later in the fourth quarter. They say a triple-play of job growth, wage gains and a strong stock market should encourage consumers to spend liberally this holiday season.

Lee Youngdahl, economist at Aubrey G. Lanston & Co Inc, forecast a modest 0.5 percent retail sales gain in October. Deleting car transactions, sales might have risen slightly less than 0.5 percent after a 0.4 percent September gain, he said.
Youngdahl is among the economists who believe that consumers will be active in the rest of the fourth quarter.
"We've had a pullback in credit buying and consumer assets are healthy," he said. "There's good job growth, good income growth, the stock market is at record levels, and consumer confidence is high.
"I think this will translate into a very positive retail experience this holiday season."
Raphael Marrone, money market economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, believes retail sales, including or excluding auto sales, rose 0.3 percent in October.
He, too, thinks retailers should have a pretty good holiday season.

"Consumer credit numbers have been coming off for several months, suggesting that tightening credit card standards have taken their toll," said Marrone. "We think we could see a pretty good Christmas sales season, with consumers coming back a little."
At Bankers Trust, vice president and global markets economist Joshua Feinman, said he considers the October retail sales data the most important numbers of the week for the credit markets.
"The major reason that the economy slowed in the third quarter is that the consumer stayed home," said Feinman. "The wild card for the fourth quarter is whether the consumer will go shopping again."
The October retail sales report, due at 0830 EST/1330 GMT on Thursday, will be the first fourth-quarter report to offer part of the answer to this question, Feinman noted.

Feinman, forecasting a 0.5 percent rise in retail sales for October, said sales have the potential "to revive a fair bit." He added that he had "a gnawing suspicion" that September's 0.7 percent retail sales gains could be revised upward in the report coming out on Thursday.
As to the rest of the fourth quarter, Feinman foresees a somewhat livelier consumer.
"I suspect the consumer will come back in the fourth quarter and that we will get greater retail sales growth in the fourth quarter than we got in the third -- when we got almost none."
